solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Published gen in Greek article promotes 'Don Carlos', perhaps

indicators.note: the words before 'in' are placed inside the abbreviation for Greek

parts.note: a paper that ran a story published it
gen is slang for information, as is dope
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper story about Greece is said to boost a famous Verdi production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' splits the Greek abbreviation around the published and gen pieces. 'Promotes' is only a link joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Verdi's Don Carlos is a large-scale serious work in five acts, an example of the grandest operatic form.

clue.text: Dress actress shortened

indicators.note: shortened means the actress's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Greta Garbo was the Swedish film actress

explanation.surface: An actress's frock has been taken up.
explanation.definitionFit: Garb is clothing or attire, a synonym of dress as a noun.

clue.text: Statement FIFA put out — US lawyer's opposing it

indicators.note: put out suggests the letters of FIFA are disturbed and rearranged

parts.note: a DA is a District Attorney, an American prosecutor
V stands for versus, meaning against or opposing

explanation.surface: An American attorney contests a declaration issued by football's governing body.
explanation.walkthrough: FIFA is world football's governing body.
explanation.definitionFit: An affidavit is a sworn written declaration made on oath, a kind of formal statement.

clue.text: Such music is constant during party?

indicators.note: during means the following words sit within the party word

parts.note: a do is a party or social function
C is the scientific symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light

explanation.surface: A question whether one kind of music always plays at parties.
explanation.definitionFit: Disco is a style of dance music, so it names a kind of music the question points to.

clue.text: Film eccentric Swiss balloonist

parts.note: a pic is an informal word for a film or picture
a card is an eccentric or amusing person

explanation.surface: A movie about an odd Swiss man who flew balloons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eccentric' looks like an adjective describing the balloonist, but it is the noun card.
explanation.definitionFit: Auguste Piccard was the Swiss physicist who made record high-altitude ascents by balloon.

clue.text: Head of Roedean puts out a football team!

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: to put someone out is to annoy or anger them

explanation.surface: A girls' school headmistress fields a football side, to everyone's surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: Roedean is a famous English girls' boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: Rangers is the Glasgow football club, so it names a team.

clue.text: Turkey leg unfinished

indicators.note: unfinished means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a stage is a leg of a journey or race

explanation.surface: A drumstick of the Christmas bird has not been fully cooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turkey' looks like the bird whose leg it is, but Chambers gives stag for a male of various animals, including the turkey-cock.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers allows stag for the male of several creatures, among them a cock bird of that species.

clue.text: Cast husband in short trousers

indicators.note: in places the husband's letter within the shortened trousers
short means the trousers word loses its final letter

parts.note: trews are close-fitting tartan trousers

explanation.surface: A husband was spotted wearing shorts.
explanation.definitionFit: Threw and cast are both past tenses meaning hurled or tossed.

clue.text: The connoisseur among a consumer group?

definitions.text: The connoisseur among a consumer group?

parts.words: The connoisseur among a consumer group?
parts.note: a consumer here is one who consumes food, so the discerning member of a group of eaters is a lover of fine food

explanation.surface: Which member of a shoppers' association is the expert?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Consumer group' suggests a body like a buyers' watchdog; the consumers are eaters.
explanation.definitionFit: A gourmet, a judge of good food, is the connoisseur among those who eat.

clue.text: Precious stone, when held up, has sparkle, reportedly

indicators.note: in a down clue, held up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the following letters sound like the word said

parts.note: fire is brilliance or sparkle, as in a gem's fire

explanation.surface: A jewel raised to the light glitters, so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Held up' turns AS upwards to SA; 'reportedly' gives PPHIRE, spelt to sound like fire; 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A sapphire is a blue gemstone, one of the traditional precious stones.

clue.text: Boy, American, with hair swept back at the front

indicators.note: at the front places the turned hair before the American letters
swept back means the hair word is turned round

parts.note: fur is an animal's hair
US is short for American, as in United States

explanation.surface: A young American lad whose hair is brushed back off his face.
explanation.definitionFit: Rufus is a male first name, so it stands for a boy.

clue.text: A group of stars sign after church number

indicators.note: after says the sign follows the church and number letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
N is the mathematical abbreviation for number
Taurus is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: An astrologer's sign follows a church service number.
explanation.definitionFit: Centaurus is a southern constellation, a named grouping of stars.

clue.text: Recommend an Edinburgh barman?

definitions.meaning: to recommend a course of action is to speak in favour of it
in Scotland a barrister, a member of the bar, is called by this title

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to urge publicly; the noun is the Scottish term for a counsel at the bar.

clue.text: Pull muscle

explanation.definitionFit: Both words are informal nouns for influence or might, as in political clout.

clue.text: Take note of trailer housing man I fancy

indicators.note: housing means the trailer word holds the rearranged letters

parts.note: a trailer for a film is an advert for it

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate, here rearranging the letters

explanation.surface: Notice the caravan where a man I fancy lives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trailer' suggests a caravan, given the housing; it is a film's preview. 'Fancy' rearranges the man and I letters, which sit just after the opening A.
explanation.definitionFit: To animadvert is an archaic or formal verb meaning to notice or remark on, often critically.

clue.text: Make a mistake collecting travel document in port

indicators.note: collecting means the mistake word takes the document inside it

parts.note: to nod is to make a slip through inattention, as in 'Homer nods'
a visa is a document allowing entry to a country

explanation.surface: Someone slips up by picking up a passport stamp in a harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: Novi Sad is a Serbian city with a river port on the Danube.

clue.text: Dessert course cut short by bishop

indicators.note: by means the bishop's letter stands beside the shortened course
cut short means the course word loses its last letter

parts.note: a syllabus is a course of study
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop curtails the pudding course of a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course' tempts as a meal course; it is a course of study.
explanation.definitionFit: A syllabub is an old English pudding of whipped cream, sugar and wine.

clue.text: Dairy product in list boy brought round

indicators.note: brought round means the boy word goes round the list word

parts.note: a son is a boy
to list is to lean, as a ship does, which is to tilt

explanation.surface: A lad fetches something from a shopping list at the dairy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'List' looks like a shopping list; it is a ship's lean.
explanation.definitionFit: Stilton is an English blue cheese, a food made from milk.

clue.text: Lawrence, jolly good to accommodate a worker, an overbearing woman

parts.note: T. E. Lawrence, Lawrence of Arabia, gives his initials

indicators.note: to accommodate means the jolly and good letters make room for the a inside

parts.note: a jolly is slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM
an ant is the classic worker insect

explanation.surface: Lawrence is glad to take on a labourer and a domineering lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jolly good' reads as an exclamation; it is two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A termagant is a harsh, bullying shrew of a woman, a virago.

clue.text: Children's book laid out on rug

indicators.note: on in an across clue puts the rearranged letters after the rug

parts.note: a mat is a small rug

indicators.note: laid out suggests the letters are spread out in a new order

explanation.surface: A storybook is set down on a carpet.
explanation.definitionFit: Matilda is Roald Dahl's novel for young readers.

clue.text: A high-class comic actor produces a weekly magazine

parts.note: U stands for upper-class, an old British usage

indicators.note: comic means the letters of actor behave absurdly, rearranged

explanation.surface: A posh stand-up actor brings out a weekly paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Autocar is a long-running British weekly motoring periodical.

clue.text: Article associated with more complex proposition

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: complex means the letters of more are tangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A piece of writing linked with a more intricate argument.
explanation.definitionFit: A theorem is a mathematical statement to be proved, a formal proposition.

clue.text: Send male out in carriage

indicators.note: out means the male letter is removed from the send word

parts.note: to transmit is to send

explanation.surface: Expel the man who is in the coach.
explanation.definitionFit: Transit means conveyance or carrying of goods or people, as carriage does.

clue.text: Henry, strangled by a blighter turning over holiday home

indicators.note: strangled by means the Henry letter is gripped inside the other letters
turning over means the a and blighter words are read backwards

parts.note: a cad is a rotter or blighter
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Henry is throttled by a scoundrel who wrecks his country retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning over' reverses A CAD to DACA, and H goes in before its last A.
explanation.definitionFit: A dacha is a Russian country cottage used for weekends and holidays.

clue.text: Copper to marry an attractive girl

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
to tie the knot is to marry, so tie means wed

explanation.surface: A policeman weds a pretty young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman; it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutie is an informal word for a pretty, appealing person.

clue.text: Hothead showing sign of emotion at opponent's ground

parts.note: a tear shows sadness or joy
a team playing at its rival's ground is playing away

explanation.surface: A crying fan at an away match is a reckless one.
explanation.definitionFit: A tearaway is a wild, reckless young person, an impetuous firebrand.

clue.text: Leading Greek character found in sacred river close to Olympia

parts.note: Alph is the sacred river in Coleridge's poem Kubla Khan

indicators.note: close to means the end letter of the word

explanation.surface: A Greek hero is discovered in a holy river near Olympia.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpha is the first letter of the Greek alphabet, which leads the rest.

clue.text: Fish tea, daily

definitions.meaning: old British slang for tea, from Chinese cha
a daily is a cleaning woman, a charwoman

explanation.definitionFit: Three separate senses: a lake fish, a slang word for a cuppa, and a cleaning lady who comes in each day.

clue.text: A scout, 10, nervous in court

indicators.note: nervous suggests jittery, agitated letters, rearranged

parts.note: the number 10 is written as ten

explanation.surface: A young scout aged ten is jittery playing on court.
explanation.definitionFit: En-tout-cas is a trade name for a hard all-weather tennis court surface.

clue.text: Beginning to prune every single tree

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: every single one means each

explanation.surface: Start by trimming each and every tree in the orchard.
explanation.definitionFit: A peach is a fruit tree as well as its fruit.

clue.text: Row in river, avoiding the middle

indicators.note: avoiding the middle means the central letter of the river is left out

parts.note: the Tiber is the river of Rome

explanation.surface: Rowing on a river while steering clear of the centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like rowing a boat; it is a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is one rank or line of seats raised above another.

clue.text: Measuring device for farm vehicle

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
a tractor is the farm vehicle

explanation.surface: An instrument for measuring things on a farm machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A protractor is an instrument for measuring angles.
